# Claude Mods and Temporal composition discovery

Status: research proposal, 2026-10-08. No executor, experiment, install, runtime upgrade, model request, credential access, infrastructure operation, contact, commit or push. Initial independent report was completed before reading the other new Mods reports. The challenge revision below records those later reads and a corrected state attribution. Original discovery-20261007 is unchanged.

## Recommendation and retained evidence

Treat Mods first as optional observation over the existing SDK runner and exact original pending recovery route. Explore interception/result shaping and inference boundary capture as separate qualification candidates. Neither becomes execution authority merely because a hook can answer an event.

Read the copied candidate spec.md, plan.md, evidence.json and plan-evidence.json; the reference application's root README; current `_runner.py` and `_workflow.py`; existing `write_recovery.py` and `write_recovery_workflow.py`; the canonical historical Mods loading probe `experiments/mods.py`, evidence.md comparison/closure sections, and the workspace `sources/2026-10-01-recovery-candidates.md`. The checkout root is `<repo>`. These source reads establish current seams, rather than a new installed-package provenance claim.

The current canonical evidence states selected SDK 0.2.162/CLI 2.1.274 original pending recovery PASS within the bounded accepted contract. Legacy synthetic injected recovery and unsafe permission configurations remain DEFECT. Do not combine those dispositions into a universal failure or treat a Mods proposal as replacing the PASS. The earlier Mods probe used SDK 0.2.154/CLI 2.1.274 and did not establish loading; it remains an unsupported tested invocation, not a verdict on a later qualified Mods engine.

`ClaudeAgentSdkRunner` construction checks conditional session append and SDK recovery fields. `_start` refuses `attempt != 1` and fork when pending recovery is enabled; engine options set serial recovery. Workspace, authoritative outcomes and host ownership remain caller responsibilities. The retained proof controller commits `proof_segment`, waits for dispatch, executes its fixed effect, then recovers from accepted outcome. It uses maximum_attempts=1 and is expressly not a general executor. Its cleanup/admission receipts are bounded evidence, not distributed host death proof.

## Primary contract observations

The [official announcement](https://claude.dev/blog/getting-started-with-claude-code-mods/) describes observe/rewrite/answer middleware and requires CLI 2.1.287 or later. Runtime emitted types are authoritative; this is distinct from the [pinned declaration](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/types/claude-code.d.ts), whose header says 2.1.277 and early access. This mismatch mandates separate exact-runtime qualification.

Pinned declaration findings: `tool.call` can answer without `next`, with native output validation/mapping; original ID/tool/agent identity is reserved. `$.tool.call` makes its own ID. Hook failure/budget expiry can continue core; `.catch` is optional. `turn.step` streams, exposes model/effort rather than a complete request, and each `next` is another request. Partial emitted chunks persist after failure. Session message summaries omit some opaque state and are bounded. `$.store` persists local JSON across sessions, capped at 4 MiB. Plugin initiated calls can skip the originating hook. These are declaration contracts, not runtime proof. Relevant sections are ToolCallInput/ToolCallResult, ToolCallArgs, HookBudget/TraceOutcome, StreamNext/StreamHook, TurnStepInput/TurnStepChunk, session.messages and store.

Correction after challenge: the initial paragraph incorrectly attributed `$.state` to the supplied pin. Session-host reload persistence for `$.state` belongs to the current announcement; the pin has neither this noun nor PluginState. Treat current-announcement state and pinned local store as separately evidenced capabilities until exact-runtime generated declarations reconcile them. Neither establishes cross-host recovery or durable acknowledgement.

The [Mods README](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/52c76441cae91f6891e4712306bffb057ff6fec5/mods/README.md) provides the public reference source and early access context. Loading through the selected Python SDK, headless mode, actual event coverage, hook precedence, serial pending recovery and compatibility with validated Skill options all remain unqualified. Existing validated package rules exclude arbitrary plugins; research does not authorize weakening that admission boundary.

Actual Temporal Docs calls establish: [Workflow replay](https://docs.temporal.io/workflows#how-workflow-replay-works) reconstructs deterministic control and reuses committed Activity outcomes; replay does not invoke a completed Activity again. [Activity idempotency](https://docs.temporal.io/activity-definition#idempotency) remains necessary if an effect succeeds and the Worker dies before completion is recorded. [Cancellation](https://docs.temporal.io/activity-execution#cancellation) may be ignored by Activity code; heartbeats communicate cancellation and are not host termination authority. The [long Activity guide](https://docs.temporal.io/design-patterns/long-running-activity) supports bounded progress/cancellation design, not stop-the-world guarantees. Model and filesystem operations belong outside deterministic Workflow code.

## Composition alternatives

| Candidate | Useful composition | Decision and required boundary |
|---|---|---|
| T1: optional observer | `tool.call` observation, `turn.step` stream forwarding, turn/session summaries feed a redacted external journal and progress UI; existing runner/controller owns defer/accept/effect/recover | Reference first. Observation never authorizes dispatch, repairs missing state or proves zero effects. Missing observer may reduce telemetry while independent controls still prevent effects. |
| T2: Mods interception plus existing pending adapter | Mod identifies/holds offered calls; existing segment controller seals original pending state, commits receipt, dispatches existing effect seam, then existing SDK adapter answers the original call | Conditional exploration. No documented durable suspend handshake was found. A deny settles an error, not an unresolved pending call. Qualification must show exact pending transcript, cessation of owned execution and accepted segment boundary before dispatch. |
| T3: native result projection | Mod maps an already accepted authoritative outcome into the original native result schema, while SDK and controller retain ownership, session and effect safety | Conditional exploration. Potential benefit is native Read/Edit metadata fidelity. Prove original ID/result pairing and postimages through actual headless SDK. Never use `$.tool.call` to reissue a completed effect or forge original identity. |
| T4: inference result escrow | Observe/buffer `turn.step` output, externally persist complete accepted inference response plus opaque compatible session prefix; promote a durable turn receipt through existing segment Activity | Exploratory design only. This might reduce recomputation after a model answer, but current surfaced summaries/chunks are not shown to be lossless provider/session escrow. Future proof must preserve native SDK entry and avoid a replacement agent loop. |
| T5: synchronous hook-to-Temporal execution | Hook calls bridge, starts/awaits tool Activity, then answers original tool | Reject as a drop-in route. Tool may run before the enclosing segment result is committed; a remote accepted operation outlives hook timeout or host loss. Making bridge a durable Workflow does not itself accept a sealed original segment. |
| T6: whole SDK segment as Activity | Existing SDK/CLI stays inside segment Activity; Temporal owns its accepted result and later effect Activities | Reuse selected architecture. Completed segment replay is safe, but uncommitted segment retry is not exact pending recovery. Preserve one attempt and explicit park/reconciliation. |

T2 and T3 could ultimately combine, but qualifying result schemas does not qualify suspension, and qualifying suspension does not qualify lost-host recovery. A live continuation that queries an accepted ledger still needs exclusive owner admission and prior termination. Bridging with asynchronous Activity completion can remove a blocked Worker thread, yet does not change the application acceptance, ambiguous-effect or ownership obligations. No alternate executor is proposed.

The [official Vercel AI SDK recipe](https://docs.temporal.io/ai/cookbook/ai-sdk-by-vercel-typescript) is useful prior art: `temporalProvider` wraps model invocation in an Activity, with model and tool Activities appearing in history. Reuse its acceptance principle as a reference for T4. Replacing the mandatory Claude SDK/native Skill runner with that loop is outside this task. A durable tool proxy or a recorded provider result does not automatically recover the Claude subprocess's exact trajectory, pending call, files or ownership. That gap is precisely what MT-4, MT-6 and MT-7 must falsify.

## Proposed durable boundaries

Use the candidate's existing ordered protocol: SDK segment yields original pending request; drain mutations and stop owned execution; durably acknowledge opaque ordered session prefix, workspace/package/claims inventory and sealed receipt; accept receipt through committed segment completion; only then permit effect Activity. Revalidate exact accepted identity and termination, write independent nonrollback intent and protected claims before spawn, durably store known result and postimages, then recover the same pending call through conditional append before a new CLI/model continuation. Known orphan result may be adopted only after exact accepted-dispatch/state reconciliation. Unknown Bash stays PARKED with no fabricated result or resumed model action.

For T4, distinguish three thresholds: displayed partial chunk, external journal acknowledgement, and accepted complete turn receipt. Only the last could become promised recoverable inference progress. The journal may be useful before acceptance but cannot silently substitute for it. Its proposed key binds original lineage/session/checkpoint, model/runtime/package fingerprints, turn position and response digest; it cannot derive execution authority from a regenerated model ID. Store raw compatible session prefix separately from redacted summaries. Capture tool input JSON after completion, including native defaults, rather than treat streamed fragments as a dispatchable request.

Inference-only recomputation before an accepted boundary may spend again or produce a different answer. That is a separate offered failure contract. A turn that has any authorized effect cannot be freely recomputed. Request escrow must include the actual effective request or a demonstrated lossless equivalent, response blocks and engine retry/fallback behavior; `turn.step` request knobs and message summaries alone do not establish that equivalence. Effect safety remains gated even if the inference journal ACK is lost or the stream hook falls back midresponse.

Host loss requires independent trajectory/workspace/intent authorities and qualified old-host terminal containment. Temporal history survives only the selected service fault domain; a local dev server or local store lost with the host does not qualify recovery. No heartbeat, TTL, detached volume, absent Pod or expired hook proves descendants or in-flight remote requests stopped. Preserve pending Agent/Task and plugin-spawned child denial through independent admission, not only a fail-open Mod.

## Falsifiable future qualification

Every row below is a proposed test, not executed evidence. Use fresh approved reservations and the existing runner/controller test seams after explicit later execution authorization.

| ID | Required observation | Failing mutation or counterexample |
|---|---|---|
| MT-1 SDK admission | Exact approved SDK/CLI/plugin/generated-type hashes; actual headless SDK loads marker Mod and original policy still admits validated Skill | Plugin absent despite successful CLI launch, arbitrary plugins allowed, or compatibility inferred from source/types only |
| MT-2 preventive fallback | Missing/disabled/throwing/overbudget/malformed hook and competing plugin leave zero physical unrecorded effects; denied child/MCP/process/fs/http paths cannot escape | Remove independent ask/permission/substrate guard; physical recorder must detect the formerly blocked mutation |
| MT-3 commit ordering | Kill before/after pending seal and segment completion; zero physical effects before accepted segment history boundary | Hook starts bridge Activity before segment acceptance; observer log is mistaken for history acceptance |
| MT-4 original pending | Replacement receives exact original ID/name/canonical input and known success/error/types without a new effect; no fabricated unknown response | `$.tool.call` reissues, deny settles the pending call, changed input/default, ordinary conversation or synthetic injected fallback |
| MT-5 attempts | Activity attempt two and fork refuse before SDK startup; maximum_attempts=1 remains; a proposed new first-attempt lineage cannot forget unresolved intent | Remove attempt guard, Reset/Continue-As-New changes lineage or clears claims to permit second spawn |
| MT-6 stream/inference | Kill at every chunk, final response, journal ACK, accepted turn and next-model barrier; accepted complete response survives with one logical accepted answer; incomplete response has explicit nonaccepted disposition | Double `next`, mixed fallback suffix, omitted thinking/tool/error/native metadata, changed provider request or acknowledged data loss |
| MT-7 trajectory | Full opaque prefix/CAS head recovered after losing owner disk; conflicting UUID, stale head and missing accepted prefix refuse | Restore only `$.store`/summary or re-create a missing session as new |
| MT-8 ambiguity | Effect recorder witnesses one Bash spawn; lose outcome and roll workspace/claims back before spawn witness; independent intent keeps PARKED with zero further effect/model calls | Native Mod fallback spawns again, clears claim or supplies an unknown result |
| MT-9 lost owner | Partition old control while preserving effect egress; replacement denied until authoritative terminal containment; remote request issued before death remains uncertain unless outcome is definitive | Lease/heartbeat expiry authorizes replacement, descendant escapes, or terminal receipt erases uncertainty |
| MT-10 projection | Actual native Read/Edit/Bash errors are compared at tool record, model-visible block, transcript and postimage levels through replacement | Only text equality tested; wrong JSON types or schema mismatch trigger core fallback |

## Retrieval accounting and limitations

Applied `temporal:temporal-developer` and read its core determinism and AI patterns references. Discovered the actual deferred `mcp__temporal_docs__search_temporal_knowledge_sources` signature through ALL_TOOLS, then called it three times. Call 1 queried retries/heartbeat/cancellation/side effects, with tool response retained in conversation only. Call 2 queried timeout/cancellation/replay; its official-doc subset is [temporal-docs-2.json](temporal/temporal-docs-2.json). Call 3 queried effect success before lost completion; its official-doc subset is [temporal-docs-3.json](temporal/temporal-docs-3.json). Captures omit nonprimary/internal retrieval results and use Unicode JSON escapes without changing decoded official snippets.

Ran three actual repo-local Atlas queries, never direct checkout reads: `Temporal Activity retries cancellation heartbeat side effects idempotency Claude agent SDK`; `Temporal cancellation timeout cannot stop activity idempotent side effects`; `Temporal durable Activity external side effect succeeds Worker crash before completion idempotency`. Final response is [atlas-query-3.json](temporal/atlas-query-3.json); earlier responses are conversation-only. Atlas supplied generic Activity/idempotency discovery rather than a Mods acceptance/recovery contract. Primary docs and exact application sources own those claims.

The report establishes source-grounded options and test obligations only. No guarantee is promoted from declarations, successful retrieval, historical scoped PASS, or a drafted test. Adoption and exact engine/SDK qualification remain open.

## Crosschallenge revision

Read [surface.md](surface.md) and [adversarial.md](adversarial.md) only after finishing the independent report. Agreement: SDK loading must be measured through the actual validated runner; mandatory accepted segment completion precedes any effect; native mapping and exact original opaque result recovery need separate oracles; fail-open hooks require independent prevention. Surface's current-source inventory adds the latest generated-declaration commit `684800b206824dfd0cc8a876e8604b20f72c3617`, still labeled 2.1.277, and native built-in/security Mod prior art. This corroborates a freshness qualification problem rather than a universal Mods rejection. I have not independently retrieved that latest commit in this lane.

Refinement: a blanket claim that long remote waits necessarily exhaust the Mod's own-code budget is unsupported. Surface distinguishes waits on `$`/lower middleware from own work and clock waits. T5's rejection is therefore based on acceptance ordering, unresolved ownership and ambiguous effects, not an assumed ten-second wall limit. A later proved suspension/acceptance bridge could change that verdict while retaining every invariant.

Adversarial's MA-11/MA-12 strengthen MT-6: accepted response must be compared against actual emitted/recorded blocks, including opaque/signed thinking behavior, not only a final `TurnStepResult` or joined text. MA-04 strengthens MT-1: actual startup activation matters even if plugin validation succeeds. MA-08/MA-17 strengthen MT-2: capability paths and permission-chain seating must be independently restricted; sec-default's scoped conservative catch is useful reference rather than complete mediation. A single unauthorized effect is a failure even without a duplicate.

Prior-art comparison: official built-in Mods demonstrate local chain interception/result handling; official Vercel integration demonstrates durable provider/tool Activity outcomes; current Claude runner/proof controller demonstrates bounded exact original pending recovery. These solve different boundaries. Synthesis should retain T1 as lowest-disruption option and T2/T3/T4 as independently gated research candidates, never infer Claude trajectory recovery from Vercel model Activities or infer durable acceptance from a Mod result.
